findings.summary: A refused first-run setup reports only its status, not which refusal fired
findings.recommendation: instance: step 5's POST /api/setup/complete is fetched with `-o /dev/null`, so a 400 prints only `finishing the guest's first-run setup answered 400`. On a fresh guest that 400 has at least three distinct causes the server names in the body's `code` (ENGINE_REQUIRED when the server cannot see soak-stub on its PATH, OPT_OUT_REFUSED when the bind or a Caddy login rules out no-login, BAD_REQUEST), and errorResponse does not log them server-side. The operator must reproduce the call by hand to learn which. Capture the body (e.g. `-o "$tmpfile"`) and include its `code`/`error` in the refusal; add the body to the 400 case of the existing refusal test.

findings.summary: install -d re-owns an existing operator-chosen SOAK_BIN_DIR to root:wheel
findings.recommendation: instance: BSD `install -d -o root -g wheel -m 0755` applies owner and mode to a directory that already exists, so a guest.conf that points SOAK_BIN_DIR at an existing non-root directory (e.g. /opt/homebrew/bin) has it chowned to root. Harmless for the default /usr/local/bin on a disposable guest; if it matters, create only when missing (`[ -d "$SOAK_BIN_DIR" ] || sudo -n install -d ...`). No edit required.
